mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero or are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month by > 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly negative at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decrease of at least 0.25 percentage points in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a monthly increase of at least 0.5% in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals a monetary policy lag effect, where easing is insufficient to offset inflation, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops >= 0.25pp AND CPIAUCSL rises >= 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative or are positive in more than 35% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of at least 5% in real personal savings (RSAFS) combined with a concurrent monthly decline of at least 2% in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a shift from consumption to saving, implying lower near-term demand and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > +5% AND GDPC1 < -2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative or are positive in more than 30% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) increase of less than 50,000 persons for three consecutive months signals labor market stagnation, which reduces consumer spending power and corporate hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50,000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative or are positive in more than 45% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: An annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for two consecutive quarters signals weak macroeconomic momentum, which depresses corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 1% annualized for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative or are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.
